_what: Synthetic Dart closure-binder gate for #3903 (DART-11), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution and bench/dart-deferred-imports: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, with ratios as the only timing gates. Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Dart ScopeResolver and pubspec loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a function misses an expected CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. small = 128 functions x 3 closures, large = 512 x 3 (functions 4x), dense = 128 x 12 (closures per function 4x; in `nested`, nesting depth 4x). Expected edges per function are computed from the binder rule, not read back from the graph: an untyped rebinding `(cs)` declines (`receiver-type-unresolved/untyped-binder`), a typed `(Other cs)` reaches Other.save, and `(x) { cs.run(); }` reaches the nearest `cs` (the `Address` parameter side by side, the enclosing `Other cs` when nested). The merge-base on main (09665c5a9 and 5d6e5c4f4 alike) misses or mis-targets those edges (for example 64 missing and 128 wrong at 64 x 3 side by side), so this gate fails without #3903.
_fingerprint_note: Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason/detail, file, name, position). Identical at the #3903 heads ecd25da87 and 82c585d89 (the replay onto main after #3882), so #3882's deferred-import change does not touch these workloads.
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_4n/t_n)/4: about 1 is linear, about 4 is quadratic. 1.5 (bench/scope-capture) wherever main is linear; 2.2 (bench/ruby-gem-resolution) only on the two nesting-depth ratios, where main is already super-linear: from depth 3 to 24, main's capture time has a fitted exponent of 1.46 (1.32-1.61), 2.6 -> 3.1 per depth doubling.
_depth_note: nested_capture_closure_scaling_ratio is the one ratio near its budget, and part of it is new in #3903: from depth 3 to 24 the capture exponent is 1.63 (1.49-1.76) with #3903 against 1.46 on main, 6609 ms against 4506 ms at depth 24 x 256 functions. attachDartLexicalNames calls synthesizeDartReceiverBinding for every closure scope that no enclosing scope binds `this` for, which is every closure under a top-level function, and that walks .parent up to the root (findEnclosingTypeDeclaration): O(depth) per closure, O(depth^2) per nest. At depth 48 it was 9.1 s of 16.6 s capture time in a profile. Carrying the enclosing type (or its absence) down the scope chain removes the climb. At depth 48 (256 functions) neither main nor #3903 produces Function nodes for the file, so sweeps stop at 24.
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.
_negative_controls_note: A root climb per binder in recordDartLexicalName (a temporary edit of languages/dart/captures.ts; the #1848 shape) fails nested_capture_closure_scaling_ratio 2.324 > 2.2 in the CI profile, with unchanged fingerprints (2.729 at 82c585d89 and 2.66 at ecd25da87 under the full protocol at the earlier 256/1024 shapes). Replacing the per-binder scope map lookup with a scan of every registered scope (O(binders x scopes)) added about 300 ms at 1024 x 3 but moved no ratio past its budget (sibling function 1.307): that is below what the gate resolves at these sizes. These are deliberate regressions, not baseline observations.

_measured_ci.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 7-40 on 15 cores)

_measured_full.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 7-40 on 15 cores)

_measured_note: Three CI-profile runs and one --full run at 82c585d89. Scalar ratios and millisecond values are per-metric maxima across the runs of that profile (rounded). peak_rss_mib (--full only) is each --shape child's high-water mark after one worker parse and one resolution, worker thread included; context, not gated. Exact shapes and fingerprints were identical in all runs. The doubling sweep in the PR comment (functions 256 -> 4096, closures 3 -> 48, depth 3 -> 24, three rounds, main 5d6e5c4f4 and #3903 82c585d89) was measured separately with --shape --reps 3 --warmup 1 and is part of neither profile.
